fields.text: The Belka Problem
lines: The Belka Problem

fields.text:
To the northwest of us is a looming threat: Belka. The militarist nation and its ability to exert an extreme amount of hard power on the Osean continent has been an ever-present danger to us and other North Osean nations. Historically, however, the Belkans have not had a strong Osea to fight and we might finally have a chance at putting an end to the Belkan menace.

On the other hand, the Belkans have been known to pull through even at the most unexpected times and siding with the Oseans might result in our own destruction in the long-term.

fields.text: The [FROM.GetName] has formally announced to us and to their own populace that they've decided to forgoe their claims on the disputed territory of Futuro in a broader effort to normalize relations between our two countries.

fields.text: Our Friends In Oured
lines: Our Friends In Oured

fields.text: The Oseans have been a strong ally of ours for ages, both thanks to aligning interests and to our mutual benefit from the amount of trade going between each others' ports. As we approach the turn of the century, many of our foreign policy establishment has been concerned about Osea's pivot towards focusing on Yuktobania and Verusa rather than the Belkans here in northern Osea. In the future, it might be the case that the Oseans will be too distracted to help us against the Belkans and we might need to consider forming our own alliance to fight a possible Belkan invasion with.

lines: Sapin Announces Military Exercise With Osea

Both nations seem hopeful about the upcoming exercises as Sapinish military personnel land in Osea to begin. The spokesperson for the Osean Defense Forces has stated the maneuvers will be dubbed "OSAP [GetYear]."

lines: Sapin Announces Independent Foreign Policy

fields.text: Sapin has announced that it is planning to readjust its foreign policy to be more independent from foreign influence, due to changing times in the world. Part of its announcement included some signalling that it might look to create its own defensive pact in Northern Osea for the purposes of collective North Osean security without being subject to the whims of Osea, Yuktobania, or Belka.

fields.text: Formation Of NOTO
lines: Formation Of NOTO

fields.text:
The [FROM.GetName] has announced the formation of the North Osean Treaty Organization (NOTO) as an independent military alliance designed for the collective security of North Osea.

This is a sharp turn away from traditional Sapinish policy, which has always been in favor of close ties between Sapin and Osea due to the nations' aligned interests and shared trade. Such a move suggests Sapin might not trust in Osea's ability to adequately protect Sapin and North Osea or possibly even Sapin's desire to be a major world player in its own right.

fields.text: Joining NOTO?
lines: Joining NOTO?

fields.text: A Sapinish delegation has arrived in our capital offering for us membership in the newly-created North Osean Treaty Organization. Should we join, we'd lose a lot of positive relations with Osea and Belka but would be entering a greater North Osean defensive pact.

fields.text: Our Perbla Position
lines: Our Perbla Position

fields.text: The Kingdom of Perbla in southern Osea is a sort of "Hermit Kingdom," mostly diplomatically isolated from the rest of the world aside from some lukewarm relations with Belka due to their hostile foreign policy. In spite of this, Perbla is a bastion of the "Ancient Regime," a monarchy that clings to the same values that our state was founded on.

fields.text: Our Border Policy
lines: Our Border Policy

fields.text: Sapin is known as being a nation historically friendly to immigration and being a nation that many North Oseans desire to move to to find better opportunities. In recent years, however, more nationalist elements of Sapinish politics have created this notion that immigrants from North Osea could be secret Belkan agents trying to undermine Sapin's national security and those who aren't are stealing jobs from hardworking Sapiniards. Attempting to address this issue, the Sapinish government has tried to tighten immigration restrictions without being too restrictive. However, this has just caused pro-immigration activists to be upset with the Sapinish government without fully placating the other side. As the head of the country, [ROOT.GetLeader] can make a royal decree addressing this issue.

fields.text: Republican Revolt
lines: Republican Revolt

fields.text: Dissatisfied with the Sapinish government's right-wing policies, the more radical elements of Sapin's Republican movement have taken up arms against the Sapinish government, proclaiming the creation of a Sapinish Republic to create the egalitarian society they desire.

fields.text: Nationalist Revolt

fields.text: South Belkan Cities Demilitarize
lines: South Belkan Cities Demilitarize

fields.text: Following a continued lack of success in our military campaign, and growing weary of the constant bombings, casualties, and state of war, almost all major cities and townships in South Belka have agreed to surrender and demilitarize, refusing to host soldiers or produce war-related products. Unable to reinforce in these cities, we have been forced to retreat, begrudgingly allowing the Osean Army to move through these territories unimpeded. While not shattering, this is a major setback and represents a large portion of our country effectively taken over by the enemy, which we will now have to reclaim. We have already prepared defensive positions in the north and are drafting new battle plans, even some rather extreme ones. Despite this precedent, and the now-constant stream of defections to this rebel state, the fight is not over yet.

fields.text: Betrayal Of Southern Belka
lines: Betrayal Of Southern Belka

fields.text: We were warned that it would come to this. Our fatherland in her most perilous hour has been met with deceit and by members of our own People no less. When we embarked upon this crusade to liberate our stolen lands, never did we think that victory would be snatched away with such duplicity. The South lands have always been less than fully Belkan, yet we had dismissed certain comrades as being paranoid and radical for pointing out what is now obvious: that South Belka was the weak link in our national chain. Our shortsightedness and timidity has doomed the Fatherland. Now Osea and her dogs are barking at the gates and our cities burn because of our foolish mistake in letting those mixed breeds fester in their treason and cowardice. The Holy Land of our forefathers must be protected, even if it means that our supposed brethren burn, even if it means releasing the power of Seven Suns upon our soil. The price must be paid.

fields.text: Osea Moves In
lines: Osea Moves In

fields.text: Despite our insistence on "demilitarization," it appears that the Oseans have merely taken advantage of the lack of defences and are now moving through our territory. However, seeing our intentions, instead of occupying us, the Osean commanders and generals are allowing us to maintain our independence, albeit under their eyes. While this is not exactly the outcome we has hoped for, this does at least guarantee minimal suffering and damage to our homes during the last echoes of this conflict, which was our primary goal. This may end up taking a turn for the worse however, as we are unsure of what Osea will do to Belka, and us by extension, when the war is over.

fields.text: Offer from Ratio
lines: Offer from Ratio

fields.text: Following our recent acquisition of territory from Belka, our eastern neighbor of Ratio has approached us with a deal. The lands of Tyrann and Boikos are primarily Ratian in culture, as they were relatively recently conquered from them by Belka. Even after falling under our control in the Belkan Federal Law Review of 1988, Ratio has never renounced their claim on the lands, however they appear to be far friendlier to us than Belka. They have offered a deal to purchase the lands back from us for a generous price, far exceeding the actual value of the territories. This, combined with several clauses allowing us to move Ustian assets out of the land and into our core areas, and a parnership with our nation for future cooperations. This deal appears to be extremely beneficial for us, as in addition to the obvious monetary benefits, we have had extensive trouble dealing with partisan forces in the area, and as a relatively new nation in the world, the presence of another ally would be greatly valued. The only protest against this deal has come from Franek Dolas, who argues that we have spent extensive resources on the lands, and even if it was under Belkan leadership, many Ustians fought and died to conquer the land. As he argues, the strongest nation will be the one who succeeds, first it was Belka, and when they were proven weak, we rose to that position instead, and if Ratio thinks they should have the land they will need to prove their strength over us to obtain it. Aside from his ramblings, the advisory board is unanimous that this deal should be taken.

fields.text: Osea Offers Western Land
lines: Osea Offers Western Land

fields.text: We received an interesting transmission from our allies in Osea today, offering us control over our former territories that were not liberated from Belka even after the 1988 Belkan Federal Law Review. It is strange to recieve this offer from a country that does not currently own these territories, however the Oseans revealed that as a part of a trade deal with Belka, the Belkans agreed to withdraw from all other occupied territories and sell the Great Lakes territories to Osea. While we would expect Osea to take these territories and sell them to us, they have not asked for a payment or even claimed the land, and are seemingly just giving it to us for free. The only request they made was to reaffirm our friendship, which we were more than happy to do, although this does make us wonder...

fields.text: The Return of the West
lines: The Return of the West

fields.text: Following the Osean's transmission, sure enough, Belka soon retreated their armed forces from Western Ustio, allowing us to move in and take over ownership of the land. This is an unprecedented move and both widens our possibilities and responsibilities greatly. For now, however, Ustians both at home and in these new territories are rejoicing for the union with their brothers, and so soon after our own liberation to. Best of all is that not a single drop of blood was spilled for this. Perhaps when all this is over we can even maintain relations with Belka, as clearly if they are dealing with Osea, perhaps they will deal with us too.

fields.text: A Welcome Surprise
lines: A Welcome Surprise

fields.text:
"We were from the 102nd Panzergrenadiers, sir." 

Men adorning Belkan uniforms and brandishing Belkan weaponary, now deep within the Ustian mountains bearing white flags, prostrated themselves before a group of extremely confused Ustian officers. Their Belkan flags were covered in strips of dirty cloth. Weapons of all kinds were pointed at them. 

"You mean to tell me..." 

"We were Belkan Armed Forces. We no longer wish to be." 

One in particular spoke out, with a black and yellow beret brandishing the emblem of the Belkan Panzergrenadiers. It was clearly worn out, and painted over in red. 

"Are you their leader?" An Ustian officer asked. 

"Yes. Studied in Sudentor. Please forgive our trespasing, but we are of this countr-" 

"You know anything about Belkan High Command?" 

The leader of the emigres stood, stiff as ever. "Yes." 

"We"ll get you new clothes. You won"t go unemployed."

fields.text: Belkan Mobilization Along Entire Border
lines: Belkan Mobilization Along Entire Border

fields.text:
Recent intelligence assessments indicate a significant escalation of military activity along the ENTIRE borders of the Belkan Federation. This development comes amidst a backdrop of heightened regional tensions and follows a substantial military buildup observed in Belka over the past two years.

Belkan authorities have initiated a comprehensive mobilization campaign, deploying military forces and fortifying defensive positions along the entirety of the nation's border. Satellite imagery and reconnaissance reports confirm a significant increase in troop movements, equipment deployments, and construction activities along key strategic sectors of the border. However, analysis suggests that this mobilization is not purely defensive in nature; rather, it bears the hallmarks of an offensive posture.

fields.text: Ratio's Response
lines: Ratio's Response

fields.text:
In a great surprise to us, Ratio has pledged to provide vital assistance and help us in our war against Belka however possible, without directly getting involved. They justify their decision with sentiments of unity and cooperation that we shown during territorial issues from 1991, and how the peaceful entire land transition was.

As part of its commitment to support our defence efforts, Ratio has authorized the dispatch of volunteer forces to bolster the ranks of our military, providing additional manpower and expertise to strengthen the front lines. In addition, they also agreed to supply us with much-needed weaponry and military equipment, ensuring that we will have the necessary resources to effectively defend sovereignty and territorial integrity.

Furthermore, Ratio has generously offered to allow us access to a portion of its industrial infrastructure for war production purposes, providing our army with a crucial lifeline to sustain its military efforts in the face of logistical challenges and resource constraints.

We will repay this unprecedented gesture – they have our ward.

fields.text:
"Two KIA, Eight Wounded."

Colonel Marazewski poured his eyes over a set of papers on his desk. Each listed reports that had been written of a recent incident where... "Our troops fired upon Ratian troops that breeched our border." 

Crazy, that this was actually happening. 

"Not war yet, no?" The colonel shrugged. Who knew how this would develop. If it were up to him he"d stage a meeting and try to reach a peaceful settlement, with some sort of joint occupation until a referendum or whatever could be done with a final solution. 

But it wasn"t up to him; He merely had to carry out his orders. A list of orders that increased exponentially, from defending fortifications to anti-partisan activities to border control. And he very recently had been told that any provocation should be retaliated against twofold, as a"Show of strength" for the young republic, hopefully detering any future aggression. It seemed as if his jurisdiction and responsibilities were expanding ever more, with a lack of promotion or rank to show for it. Was the army that overextended? 

"Are we going to follow up sir?"

fields.text:
"The Rail lines across Tyrran, sir." 

In front of Colonel Marazewski this time, lay more papers, but instead of combat reports they were combat plans. Well, terrorist plans. Ratian partisans had created a plan to distrupt the rail links between Tyrran and Boikos, as well as the rest of the nation. Intricate, yet crudely composed, it consisted of the installation of Pipe Bombs during the night onto the rail networks, after the provocation of watchmen with rifle fire. 

"And they want to kill the guards and overrun the rail line, install the explosives, run, and set them off at peak times?" 

"That's what it says sir." 

What kind of dogs think of such things? 

"We could just heavily reinforce the various rail lines that they want to attack, but that"ll still likely get people killed... Do we know the people who are behind the operation?" 

"No sir. We have a long list of suspects, and lots of fingerprints as well as handwriting can be traced, however we do not know all the potential perpetrators. For all we know, it could be an entire suburb in Tyrann, sir." 

Arresting a group would be quite belligerent, but it would ensure no one would get hurt in the long run... Reinforcement means engagement is certain, and with the skill of the partisans, Ustian blood would be spilled. But mass arrest is quite...

fields.text: To Find A mediator
lines: To Find A mediator

fields.text:
Amidst the escalating tensions and territorial disputes with Ratio, president Naruszewicz has made a strategic decision to seek the intervention of a great power to mediate the ongoing border conflict. We are recognizing the complexity and potential volatility of the situation, so we opted to appeal to the diplomatic expertise and influence of a prominent global actor in the "hopes" of facilitating a peaceful resolution to the longstanding dispute.

If everything goes okay, the appeal for mediation will be met with optimism by the international community, and will hopefully buy us more time to get ready for imminent conflict while hiding behind "proactive" efforts to de-escalate tensions and pursue a peaceful resolution to the border dispute.

Sadly we only have two real options for a mediator on whom Ratio will agree. And both of the are rather not great...

fields.text: Mundane Deaths
lines: Mundane Deaths

fields.text:
"Two Dead, Sixteen Wounded." 

Colonel Marazewski stared into the ceiling. His eyes were pratcially lifeless. Hearing death and agony had become a regular occurance at this point. Ratian partisan resistance had evolved from isolated terrorism to an entire secret hidden insurgence campaign. The government has done a great job concealing it, much to the detriment of the president's time and mental health, but the military were just not equipped for this kind of war. 

'structural integrity of the building has been compromised. We cannot repair it quickly, we will effectively have to construct a whole new centre." 

Another building, this time a barracks for Ustian troops, had been attacked and destroyed. Thankfully, not many soldiers were around to be killed, due to a set of maneouvres the Colonel had put in place to ensure that soldiers are not easy targets for terrorism. However... 

"We need a place for those boys to sleep now."

Quite frankly, the destruction and death hurt the man's heart. The runner in front of him knew this, reading it all over his relatively pale and slowly sickening complexion. The whole ordeal was not good for the Colonel's health. 

'sir, if you don"t mind my suggestions, I"d reccomend a call for reinforcement, sir. You"d do well with some relief, and more help could mean mroe efficient patrols, sir." 

That was an option yes... But demands had already began coming in for troop withdrawal. Bringing more in would be a statement, but it was a statement that Marazewski could make...

fields.text: More Mundane Deaths
lines: More Mundane Deaths

fields.text:
'seventeen Dead, Thirtyfour Wounded." 

What the fuck!? 

"Are they fucking SERIOUS!?!?" Marazewski slammed his entire arm on the desk. The reverberations shook the room, with a couple of items falling from the desk to the floor. Among them, a rolled up message from Ratian forces requesting investigatory powers. 

"Are they crazy? What kind of sick FUCKS are they?" 

"I don"t know sir." 

"To think they"d set of bombs in cars, near military installations and law enforcement, in administration sectors, I understand that kind of resistance." 

The heated rage in the colonel's voice could be felt burning just from his words. You didn"t even have to reach forwards, the flames licked at your skin however far you"d be. 

He settled down. 

"...Of all places, a toy shopping district..." 

The room fell into a deathly silence. The colonel slumped down into his chair and buried his forehead into the palm of his hand, his eyes burning holes into the reports in front of them. Amongst the dead and injured, only one of them could be considered a suitable target, being the son of a police officer. The rest, were genuine civillian children, out shopping for gifts for the upcoming gift-giving season.

"... Sir, I don"t know, but I think we"re fighting the right fight at this point. But... What do we do about this sort of thing...?"

fields.text: A Firm Solution?
lines: A Firm Solution?

fields.text:
Marazewski, was at this point, just a general in a colonel's rank. He oversaw every detail in the east of the country, and was responsible for all the decisions taken. That being said... A very pressing decision had to be made. 

Right now. 

In his hands, partially crumpled up due to pure stress, were requests for a demilitarisation of the east. 

On one hand, the man would KILL to be transferred elsewhere. He doesn"t even know why he's still here, why the country still protected this land. 

But on the other hand... He has orders, and national pride. Can he REALLY justify any sort of dismissal of his own orders? As various as they are, he has a duty as a soldier of the nation. 

Not that he had much time to think, the offer expired quite soon. He sighed, galloped his coffee, and looked up. His trusted advisor and soldier, who was basically his second in command in all but rank at this point, stood awaiting. Ready to relay whatever the colonel wished.

 Truthfully, he also wanted to leave. He wanted to go home. He wanted to see his family and see peace. But wherever the colonel placed him, he would stay there with all his heart. It was his service, his duty, his response, to his country's gift of freedom. 

The colonel opened his mouth.

fields.text: A Firm Response?
lines: A Firm Response?

fields.text:
Marazewski sighed. It was time. He had planned for this very instance, with prayers it would never come to this. But it did. 

The past few months had revealed something abour Marazewski. He had discovered his hatred of death, his hatred of conflict, his hatred for war. Yet here he was, being the mastermind behind the operation to remilitarise Tyrann and Boikos, before conducting "Operation Backstep", a surprise attack into Ratio. 

Handpicked by Dolas too. What a big shot this guy had become. Not that anyone knew about him, or about the life of turmoil and trouble he had led so recently, stressed to his core, swamped with casualty reports. And just when he thought he got a break... 

'sir, the preperations are ready." 

Honestly, he didn"t even know if he was ready for what he was about to do. Could he stomach it? Could he really be responsible for this, bear the weight of the boulders of burdens upon his shoulders that he started this war? 

Regardless, there are duties to be fufilled, and Marazewski woudl fufill his.

fields.text: Yuktobanian Proposition Of Referendum
lines: Yuktobanian Proposition Of Referendum

fields.text:
The proposal, delivered through diplomatic channels to both Ustio and Ratio, outlines a comprehensive plan for conducting a referendum within the disputed regions. Under the proposed referendum, residents of the affected territories would be given the opportunity to democratically determine their own fate, choosing between remaining within their current nation or joining the neighboring state.

Yuktobanian officials cite the principles of self-determination and democratic governance as the driving forces behind the referendum proposal, emphasizing the importance of respecting the will of the affected populations in resolving territorial disputes. The proposal also includes provisions for international oversight to ensure the fairness and transparency of the referendum process, with neutral observers tasked with monitoring the proceedings to uphold the integrity of the vote.

The announcement of Yuktobania's referendum proposal has sparked a flurry of reactions from both Ustio and Ratio, with government officials, politicians, and citizens alike expressing a mix of cautious optimism, skepticism, and concern. While some view the proposal as a promising opportunity to peacefully resolve the border disputes and strengthen regional cooperation, others remain wary of the potential implications of diffrent outcomes of this event.

Belkan representatives emphasize the need for the nation to focus its resources and energies on addressing pressing domestic issues, rather than becoming entangled in the complexities of external conflicts.

fields.text:
Marazewski's entire body stood stright upright at attention. The breeze blew a cold steel upon his cheek, the sound of the flag gallantly waving amidst the wind, and the bittersweet taste of the moment. All extremely present senses that coated his mind, as he began his march. 

In the end, it appears, his efforts were recognised. He had kept a record of the times as a colonel in the east, and written about it all in a book,"Silence Upon the Mountin Tops'. All about him and his best friend, Jannik, who was also his effective second in command, and runner. All about their time fighting the Ratian resistance, about fighting the war in the east, and about all the weight that bore upon the two men as they ordered death after death after death. 

He approached Dolas. The man who'd given him all the clearance to act as he did. Was he really the good guy here? He fought a group of people who just wanted to join their mother country. 

He might as well be a Belkan. 

A sturdy hand was lifted, with two fingers pointed. His entire body was stiff. Was it the soldiering, or was it the stress? He stood still as a statue as the honours were pinned to him. 

The heat was finally getting to him. He recounted the dead. The numbers in his head. One KIA, Two KIA, Seventeed KIA, statistics with actual meaning behind them. 

He lowered his saluted. He performed his about turn. He could hear the flapping of the flag turning to the crackle of gunfire as he lifted his left leg to march...

fields.text: A Feeling Forgot
lines: A Feeling Forgot

fields.text:
Decades upon decades have passed without the power to lift even a finger to feed our families. Since an era long before now, our nation, our people, and our home have been subject to foreign oppression, foreign rule, from a foreign land, with our needs neglected. For a time beyond generational memory, Ustian language has been forbidden, Ustian culture has been suppressed, and Ustian families have been displaced. 

Silence upon the mountain tops. 

Call it luck, call it divine intervention, call it whatever one may. But by the grace of god, our souls, and this land, our mountians once more prevail as great fortresses of freedom. Our people sing and laugh free from the boulders of burdens they shouldered a year ago. The Belkan menace has left, and we are able to make our own decisions, be our own masters. 

The future of our nation is held now in our hands. We pull the rigging of our country and let our standard fly as we sail towards a new milenia. With one decade to go, let us make it a prosperous one, and we can look beyond decades, centuries, as long as the sun and moon last, to keep our new Ustio free from foreign tyrany.

fields.text: What is History?
lines: What is History?

fields.text:
Let the Belkan recount the tale of the glorious knights around the table, as they charaded and ventured across Waldreich and cleansed the land of evil. Let the Osean speak of the times of trade, when commerce and kings came together over capital, sharing prosperity with one another. Let the Erusean speak of struggle, as they bludgon nad bleed their path across time. Let the Yuktobanian speak of strife, as man and monarch clash for control over who gets to eat and who will freeze. 

But timeless turbulance has left us without a mouth to tell our tale. To tell the tale of our states of old, of our myths and manners, of our folklore and facts across the ages. We had no hand to write the stories of the highlanders and their accounts. We had no limbs to move or dance to our songs of the great dukes of yesterday. 

Let it be that with our newfound seat of power, as well as great help from collectors and popular storage, we can ensure that we give return to our culture its mouth, hands, and limbs again. Let us reclaim what was stolen from us, centuries ago.

fields.text:
The mayor trembled as he looked upon the tremendous crowd before him. 

How long ago was he one of the many imprisoned, accused and convicted of the crime of intellect? How long ago was he struggling to bargain with Belkan officials to try and put a loaf of bread on his plate for just one more week? It can"t have been more than a good five years, give or take a couple more, can it? God no, things had escalated so rapidly that he was begining to stiff up. 

The crowd themselves were deathly silent. Quite the serious aura was afloat, an atmosphere so heavy it could be cut with a knife, and seemingly just waiting to explode. How many were there out in front of the ribbon-bound gates anyways? Certainly uncountable amounts, and then some. Every single Ustian knew exactly what this new building meant. It signalled a new light, a beacon of hope, shining back at them from history straight into their eyes. 

The mayor turned to the red ribbon adorning the gates. Within his pocket, scissors. As he picked them up, his hands trembled. What was it, excitement? Was it fear of what was to come? Was it grief for those who have gone, or was it something else entirely? Some patriotic fervour mixed in with being in the right place at the right time... 

 He cut the ribbon. And in an instant...

"One KIA, Seven Wounded." 

Colonel Marazewski gritted his teeth. Tasked with guarding the ex-Belkan fortifications as they underwent renovations, a particular thorn in his side reared its ugly head the moment he began his work. 

 "Zero structural damage received, zero damage caused to the enemy. They withdrew to an unknown location." 

Right, they had some sort of hiding spot somewhere. God knows where, there were a million small houses and villages dotted and unmarked on any map. 

"It's like we"re not even in our own country, sir." 

"Honestly..." The colonel sighed. "You might be right. It's only been a week since we began, and the fatalities they"ve caused have been more efficient than anything we ever mounted against the Belkans." 

Ratian separatism was basically a given in a staggaring amount of communities in Boikos and Tyrann. With Belka weakened, the lands fell under Ustian administration. But this was not an option for a large portion of the population, and upon the news that Ustio were rennovating fortifications there, attacks began, and only became more sporadic. 

"I don"t want to expend more energy and divert more men than I must. For all I care, our job is to just let these forts be done, but by god..."

fields.text:
'seventeen KIA, Eighteen wounded." 

Marazewski didn"t even look up to the one relaying the numbers. His eyes fixated at a map, with bunkers, trenches, foxholes and entire defensive systems dotted across it. One major label, "Tyrann", lay next to a large patch of lines representing the industrial city. Near the middle, the administrative centre lay. Fresh red ink encircled the marking, with a small statement next to it, in note form. 

'structural damage is reparable, but emergency services are struggling to arrive on site due to a nationalist riot. We have inflicted rounded up some perpetrators and five others were killed. Many escaped." 

The Colonel's hands clenched to fists. He could feel he was unwanted where he was. He could feel the prejudice against him. He could feel the fire of the flames that crackled over the remains of the administrative centre. 

It's not like this incident was isolated, though it was by far the worst case they"ve been dealt yet. Police and Armed Forces had been fired upon, and many depots had been raided. This attack was unprecedented and on a scale beyond what anyone would expect, but it's not like it hadn"t been built up to. 

"You know sir... It's like us." 

"What do you mean?" 

"They"re like us sir. The Belkans also built factories, and developed our country in the cities, to fuel their homeland. They just don"t like a foreign ruler, they don"t want us as foreign masters, sir." 

The Colonel looked up at his messenger, his eyes almost lifeless.

"Zero KIA, Zero Wounded."

Marazewski laid his head back, staring at the ceiling. The man opposite continued the report. "No reactionary movements were spotted. The deal went unhitched. Effective tommorow, the land will be under joint occupation, and the day after, where we stand will be under Ratio's jurisdiction." 

The colonel tilted his head left, taking in the sight around him. He wouldn"t remain here for long. His job was done, his mission was... Somewhat successful? Somewhat not, but he couldn"t care less. 

'so, peace, huh? We give them back this stolen land, and go back to our country. They get what they want, we get peace." He sighed. 

"Yes sir. If you don"t mind me commentating, in my opinion, the best outcome sir." 

The best outcome. The occupiers retreat, the occupation ends, the peace restored. Sure did seem like the best outcome. The colonel could at least maybe finally get some shuteye. 

'sir, if you also don"t mind me adding on, I request that you get some sleep sir. Your eyes are bloodshot and your face is red. Your body is tense. There are, I"ve counted, At least Eighteen cups of coffee that have been fully emptied on the desk to your right, sir. I don"t think this is good for morale or for your health sir." 

The colonel chuckled. "Thanks for always being here and helping me, Janek. I"ll put in a good word. I"m indebted, you could say..." 

Janek relaxed his shoulders slightly, and smiled at the colonel.

Across inns, pubs, housing and hotels, all eyes were glued on one form of screen or another, all relayed the same information, and all holding their breath. 

After decades without a voice, the Ustian people finally got their voice. And they were about to be bombarded with placation, promises, and preaching from the candidates that they would eventually choose. 

What did it feel like, to have power finally? Many felt strong, many were scared, and many were just happy that they no longer had to rely on a whim in Dinsmarck to live. But how that power would be used, and the path it would guide the nation down, would be seen in the days to come.

In all honesty, he did somewhat expect this outcome, and he wouldn"t have minded the opposite. His largest work, the birth of the republic, had been complete. Now all that remained was the security of the state, and a strong future for the people. 

Yesterday, he"d spent hours upon hours daydreaming the future, wondering just how he"d ensure he"d succeed. It's not like spacing out was particularly hard anyways, especially for a dreamer like the man himself. But to the sound of praises from the television screen as news reporters announce his victory, he simply sat and pondered the future.

fields.text:
The father of the nation slouched back in his refined chair. To the outside public, he could only ever be seen with a straight back, a stern yet strong and warm smile, as well an aura of complete trust and motivation. 

Clocks keep ticking in the corner of his room. How long had it been since his greatest work? Felt like a second and an eternity at the same time. And how long would he remain in this chair? One term? Two? Several? Would he even die in it? 

All that there is to focus on anyways, is the now. Whilst he does stay, he will ensure that every man woman and child that he can ensure the welfare of, will remain smiling for the future, unlike the times long gone. But... 

God was it so tiring.

fields.text: What is Freedom?
lines: What is Freedom?

fields.text:
"Freedom is not just a word." 

The father of the nation steadied himself. A quickly composed guideline for a speech had been hasitly redrafted several times over the past week as an address to the nation. He wished he could make it longer, he wished he could talk for years about his plans for a central efficient state, a land of no neglect, and a thwart against whatever outer powers may try to once more have their way with the mountain nation. But there was no way he"d fit every single one of his plans onto a piece of paper, and no way he"d manage to disclose all he wanted. No matter how many times he tried. 

 This was his 67th redraft. 

 "Freedom is the right of a man to live detached of dread. Freedom is NOT the ability for a man to do all he wills." 

Freedom. That was the gist of his plans. 

He"d decided to take a more metaphoric approach to his address. He wouldn"t facilitate people to do as they pleased whilst he was up at the top, but he"d make sure that people were free from the woes of society. 

"The times ahead are laced and peppered with all that is required for a future filled with freedom. Freedom from poverty. Freedom from slavery. Freedom from the overarching fear of the death of humanity within a person. That is what is to-" 

Well, he never intended on keeping it short...

fields.text:
"With co-operation we can remain independent. With independence, we can retain rights. With rights, we can achieve happiness." The father once again was mapping out his general thoughts. 

The republic had just been born a few years earlier. Not that the nation had no history, but a lot of that history involves remaining under the occupation of a large foreign northern power, the Belkan Federation. 

"...Never again." 

The vow that every man in the nation took, to never again let the Belkans crush the free spirit of the mountains. The peaks were sacred, and they had been desecrated by Dinsmark. That could just as easily happen again. 

"There's no other option. We need co-operation." 

Grzegorz never was one to shove responsibility on others, away from himself. Truthfully, he somewhat mistrusted the world after his early years, and couldn"t imagine a future for the country where he wasn"t there. But he couldn"t protect the country alone. Without help, Ustio could only rely on god to defend the nation. The Belkan army was still a formidable force, and Ustio's own was quite motivated, but reports from Dolas show an extreme lack of readiness for war. So, just in case... 

"Osean Federation. Please..."

fields.text: A Good Deed?
lines: A Good Deed?

fields.text:
"I don"t think you quite understand." 

The father of the nation buried his heads into his hands. Across his desk, was his best friend, and effective head of the armed forces, Franke Dolas, who spoke again. 

"You"re beloved by the whole nation. Your people are living a better life than they could ever have dreamt of. Your opposition can"t even lift a finger to criticise you. This is quite funnily, the most democratic step forwards."" 

Grzegorz looked down at the proposition that he had written up. He"d made thousands of bills and every single one had passed with a very firm strong majority. There was no doubt in his mind that this would follow the same path. Effectively, he was the legislative and the executive. The only question of passing legislature was if he wanted to pass it. 

"These powers are... Practically dictatorial." He stammered. "Franke, you know I actually just want to resign and retire to an estate outside of Directus or whatever." 

"They are, but they"d only last your term. When you"re done, you can just as simply go and vanish afterwards... Though I doubt you"ll live a peaceful life whatever you do." 

Dolas was right. All hopes of a peaceful life were gone the moment he gathered a following many years ago. But that wasn"t the point. 

"Do I have the right...?" 

"That's not a question for me, but for yourself." 

He knew that. He knew that whatever he did, it would be accepted. He knew it all, so why didn"t he know his answer...? 

The clocks kept ticking. He spoke up.

fields.text: Back in time?
lines: Back in time?

fields.text:
"I"m done." 

A large tall figure brandishing glasses and a physicians badge placed his coffee cup on his desk. Softly, he spoke again. 

"There's no use in arguing, everything that he does for us is the right chioce. We have had no culture, no voice, no national spirit, for centuries. It's important to reintroduce these to our youth, and he's correct. But from my end... I cannot continue to live the life I wanted in this industry if I cannot keep time with the students." 

Across from him, was his teaching assistant, who simply stood there, absorbing everything she heard, shocked. This teacher had taught the brightest youth of Ustio, bringing up entire generations of physicians. Years ago he vowed to teach until he would die. 

"I think with this, it's time for me to go back into the industry, rather than into teaching. Less time with the youth means I can"t teach as effectively. We can"t go into as heavy courses as we could under the hyper-STEM focused Belkans. I guess what I"m trying to say is..." 

"You"re a specialised heavy teacher, not a general teacher?" 

The TA hit the nail on the head with that one. "With this reform, whole national ciriculums will change. And that's okay. I just won"t be able to keep with it. Perhaps one of the final things that remained from Belkan occupation was the heavy scientific school system. If we really want to be free..."

fields.text: Against all odds...
lines: Against all odds...

fields.text:
Kuba Morkawiecki couldn"t believe it, as he sat upright in his refurbished presidential chair, taking in the sights around him. Against all odds, he had triumphed in the election against the father of the nation. Truthfully, he"d already resigned himself to a loss internally. But the business connections and promises of freedom to act and liberty of will seemed to capture the hearts and minds of the Ustian population after years of restriction. 

Perhaps this was better. Of course his opponent was a good man, and Kuba recognised this, but there was one major difference between the two. The father wanted every man to be free from agony, oppression, bondage and the like, whereas Kuba wanted every man to be free to act, produce, and live. 

Rather than a regulated shelter, the time has come for Ustio to be a shining beacon of liberty amongst the mountians. And would all all start in this chair.

lines: Mental Fortress

fields.text:
This was not at all according to the plan... 

It was meant to go like this: 
The population of Ustio votes Morkawiecki in, he gives them the deregulation they want, fufills his promises, earns the trust of the people, and everyone lives free and happily ever after. 

He did not realise just how extensively popular the social safety nets the father had set up really were. God, even proposing to get rid of one in government was a hassle to convince his own party, let alone the opposition. But he would do it. 

So he rose before he spoke and cleared his throat. A carefully prepared speech thought out, addressing the state of the republic and the path forwards. A statement endorsing liberty, capital, freedom. A statement endorsing the right of a free man to persue the happiness he wishes without being held back by any form of tyranny, malicious or benevolent. It was a clear jab at the ideals of the previous administration, and a complete gamble. fields.text:
Kuba's head was buried into his hands. He was practically bawling like a baby at this point. God, socio-economic reform after drastic changes were already made have proven so much more the challenge than expected. Even presidents have their limits. 

It's not like Kuba thought it would be easy, but with every single person in the entire nation, hell, the whole of Strangereal doubting your abilities or your plans, you can"t help but feel a bit demoralised. 

A couple more tears fell onto the desk. It"d taken whole entire days without sleep, packed with stress and paperwork, meetings, speeches, persuasion, coercion, every trick in the book to even put forwards the slightest bit of liberal economic reform. God, why did they even elect him? 

Well, he made a promise, and even if no one really wants him to follow through on that promise, he would follow through on it himself. No matter the cost.

fields.text: An Argument Against Tyranny
lines: An Argument Against Tyranny

fields.text:
"Not all presidents in future will be benevolent." Kuba recites yet another speech for yet another governing session for yet another round of lobbying, convincing, persuading, and praying, that representitives will listen to his calls to abolish tyranny. 

Not that Ustio was by any means a dictatorship, but in Kuba's eyes, there was far to much power in a central government, that could easily funnel funds straight to Directus and siphon everything else, through clever maneouvring. Such a future had to be stopped, and so here was the president, making another speech about devolution. 

"No one can be certain that another Naruszewicz will arise. He is a good man, and I have zero doubt that he has a bad bone within his body. However, his mistake as not preparing Ustio for a future where he is not steering the wheel. 

What happens then, when a malicious tyrant takes such a powerful office as the one I"m in, and promises greatness for Directus whilst neglecting the nation? I"m certain that many of you would be inclined to follow through with them, leaving the gaps within the nation wide. 

I do not want freedom to exploit. My proposal is that no one is left neglected."

fields.text: Forwards in time?
lines: Forwards in time?

fields.text:
"I"m done." 

A large tall figure brandishing classes and a physicians badge placed his coffee cup on his desk. He grinned and spoke again. 

"I"ve done it. I"ve finally done it." 

Hardly containing his excitement, he clenched his hands into fists of joy and success. Happy as a little kid, giddy as a drunken man, he breathed in and out to control and steady himself. 

"I can now die peacefully. I"ve done it! I"ve brought up my golden generation of scientists, of doctors and professors, to take my stead and move forwards, to bring Ustio into a new technological golden age. No longer do I need to abide by some strict set of rules and regulations, I can transfer everything I know to the future! I"ve done it!" 

His teaching assistant stood in front of him, visibly relieved. The teacher himself raised his chalk to the board behind him and began to scribble a set of characters. The pure happiness expressed by the man could be felt just by looking at the words. 

"And here are the grades achieved from this cohort, and the predicted from the next... It's all up for our country from here. We will never again be siphoned from intellect, we will forever be enlightened!"

fields.text: A March of Support?
lines: A March of Support?

fields.text:
Kuba stared into the television screen. This was... Unexpected. Never before had so many people at once come out to express their support for Kuba's reforms. 

Was the man dreaming? Had the day finally come, where he wouldn"t have to be the only one fighting for liberty? Shocking. 

"Morka's free-rule push is essential if we can even begin to consider ourselves a free country!" One of the marchers spoke, for once in support of the president. "To restrict a man goes against the very concept of liberty, of freedom!" 

Well yeah that was one thing, but the other was that illegal goods are just a pain in the back to regulate... But the spirit is right. 

Looks like finally, the spirit of freedom and common sense had been knocked into the people of Ustio. A future autocracy could be avoided. The republic would be a free state, for free men, living free lives.

fields.text: The Belkan War
lines: The Belkan War

fields.text:
War has broken out on the Osean continent between the Belkan Federation and the Osean Federation. Though the Oseans are out primary geopolitical rival, the Belkans are no angels either. They are, objectively, more diametrically opposed to us politically after all.

If we do not intervene, it would, at best for us, result in both Dinsmark and Oured bloodying their noses while we grow our strength. At worst for us, the Belkans win a decisive victory and we have a new geostrategic rival to deal with. One far more militarist and nationalistic than even the most hawkish Osean.

If we intervene, it will result in Yuktobania boots on the ground and pilots in the air in Osea. It will cost us a lot of resources but could result in a strong showing of Yuktobanian military prowess along with lowering the chance of a Belkan victory. However, if the Oseans lose anyway, it would be a great embarassment for us and we will have to deal with a strong Belka.
